result.summary: This PR makes cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake defensive by checking whether mpcalculator, mpprinter, and mpexample targets exist before calling set_target_properties on them, avoiding a CMake configuration error when building against a version of libmultiprocess where those targets are being removed (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#287). The change is a small, mechanical guard (+5/-1 lines) affecting only the custom/external libmultiprocess build path, not the subtree build most users and CI use.
result.problem: When Bitcoin Core is configured against an updated external libmultiprocess that removes the mpcalculator/mpprinter/mpexample example targets, cmake configuration fails with 'Can not find target to add properties to: mpcalculator'. This affects developers and CI jobs building against a non-subtree, external libmultiprocess, including the libmultiprocess project's own CI.

open_concerns: hebasto argues the underlying fragility should be fixed in the libmultiprocess subproject itself (e.g. gating example subdirectory inclusion) rather than defensively in Bitcoin Core's cmake, to avoid forcing parent projects to process CMake code they never use.
ryanofsky disagrees with hebasto's proposed alternative, citing added fragility and preferring the separate upstream fix in libmultiprocess#287; no consensus reached on which approach to take.

result.card: This draft PR adds a defensive TARGET check in cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake so configuration does not fail when an external libmultiprocess build removes the mpcalculator/mpprinter/mpexample targets, per the upstream PR bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#287. The problem only affects custom/external libmultiprocess builds and the libmultiprocess project's own CI, not Bitcoin Core's normal subtree build, as the author's description explicitly notes. hebasto gave a concept ACK but proposed fixing this upstream in the subproject instead; the author pushed back, and the discussion about the right approach stalled without resolution. The PR has been silent for over 100 days, making it Stale for review purposes. Priority within build is low (P4) given the narrow, non-default-path scope of the problem.
